flags:
# Build configuration for development and measurement in this repository.
#
# This file applies only when cargo is invoked with this directory as the working directory. It is
# not inherited by crates that depend on `zeebra`, so nothing here constrains a consumer; a
# downstream build gets whatever that build configures. See the README section "Build
# configuration" for what a consumer does and does not inherit.
#
# `x86-64-v3` rather than `native`: v3 is the Haswell/Excavator feature level (AVX2, BMI2, FMA,
# LZCNT, MOVBE), which is the floor the SIMD work in M19 targets. `native` would make a build
# artifact depend on the machine that produced it, so the same commit would benchmark differently
# on two machines for reasons that have nothing to do with the commit. Pinning the level keeps
# measurements comparable across machines and across CI runs.
#
# To measure with everything the local CPU has, override on the command line. The RUSTFLAGS
# environment variable REPLACES the flags below rather than adding to them, so repeat any flag
# that is still wanted:
#
#   RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" cargo bench
#
# Scoped by `cfg(target_arch)` and not set in `[build]`: `-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3` is not a valid
# CPU name on aarch64, so an unscoped setting would break a cross build rather than merely fail to
# help it.
[target.'cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")']
rustflags = ["-C", "target-cpu=x86-64-v3"]

# No compiler cache for this crate, measured rather than assumed.
#
# `sccache` is a reasonable default for a many-crate workspace and a poor one here, because this is
# one large crate built under `lto = "fat"` with `codegen-units = 1`. Measured on 2026-11-06, three
# `cargo build --release --lib` runs into fresh output directories with the cache warm: **44 of 48
# units hit and the wall clock did not move** — 83.1 s, 82.4 s, 79.4 s. The hits are all cheap leaf
# dependencies. The one unit that matters, `zeebra` itself, is **79.2 s of the ~83 s** and misses,
# because at least one dependency rlib is not byte-reproducible across output directories and
# `sccache` hashes `--extern` rlib *contents*, so every crate downstream of it re-keys.
#
# Worse, `sccache` is only cacheable at all with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, and that costs the edit loop
# directly: `cargo check` after a one-line change is 1.9 s at 0 against 0.7 s at 1. So the default
# trades 2.7x off the loop you run hundreds of times for 4% of a build you run occasionally.
#
# An empty string **disables** a wrapper configured further up the tree — on the development
# workstation `~/projects/.cargo/config.toml` sets one for every project under it. Note that the
# `RUSTC_WRAPPER` environment variable overrides this file, so the environment must not set it for
# this to take effect; see the README section "Build configuration".
#
# This is also the setting that prevented a class of confusing failure. A cached stale `libzeebra`
# rlib surfaces as an example failing to compile against `pub use` items that are plainly present,
# which has cost this project several debugging sessions.
[build]
rustc-wrapper = ""
